question: By exactly how much did legally mandated 60-day notice reduce earnings losses in the plant-closing study?
expected_answer: The comment describes a claim based on voluntary arrangements preceding the legislation. The abstract provides no measured effect size for the mandate.

W2130236240: Separates the statutory expectation from the voluntary evidence.

evidence.title: The Impact of Advance Notice: A Comment on a Study by Nord and Ting
evidence.quote: In their analysis of the effects of advance notification of plant closings, Nord and Ting (ILR Review, July 1991) claim that much can be expected of current legislation that mandates a 60-day prenotification standard because the outcomes of voluntary arrangements, in an interval preceding implementation of the legislation, point to substantial reductions in both joblessness and earnings losses for workers given over two months' warning of their impending layoff.
evidence.supports: Separates the statutory expectation from the voluntary evidence.

rationale: The passage invites confusion between the policy discussed and the period that supplied the evidence.
limitations: An expectation about legislation supplies neither a post-legislation estimate nor its magnitude.

question: In the multilayer study, did the magneto-optical Kerr effect increase or decrease?
expected_answer: The direction depends on sublayer thickness. The authors describe enhancement for larger thicknesses and a large reduction for smaller ones.

W2317432785: Assigns the two directions to larger and smaller thicknesses, respectively.

evidence.title: Structural and Magnetic Studies of [Co0.45Fe0.45Zr0.1/a-Si]N Multilayers
evidence.quote: These two models give a good explanation of the magneto-optical TKE effect enhancement and its huge reduction in the multilayer with larger and smaller sublayer thicknesses respectively.
evidence.supports: Assigns the two directions to larger and smaller thicknesses, respectively.

rationale: The question omits the condition that distinguishes two opposite directions in the same abstract.
limitations: A single unqualified direction would discard one of the reported regimes.

question: Among the dialysis patients whose knees improved after surgery, how many also had a clear corneal graft at their last visit?
expected_answer: The knee and eye papers report separate cohorts and endpoints. Their summaries provide no individual linkage from which to count overlap.

W3101922761: Reports graft clarity at last follow-up.

evidence.title: Perioperative Complications of Total Knee Arthroplasty in Dialysis Patients
evidence.quote: METHODS: We retrospectively assessed 21 patients (26 knees) with ESRD who underwent primary TKA between 2007 and 2015.

evidence.title: Perioperative Complications of Total Knee Arthroplasty in Dialysis Patients
evidence.quote: At the latest follow-up, 19 patients (90.5%) had improved clinical outcomes of the knee after TKA according to the American Knee Society Scores (P < .01) and Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Arthritis Index scores (P < .01).
evidence.supports: Reports improved knee outcomes.

evidence.title: Ten-Year Outcome of Glaucoma Drainage Device Surgery After Penetrating Keratoplasty
evidence.quote: METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed medical records of all patients who underwent GDD placement after PK at our institution between 2001 and 2017.

evidence.title: Ten-Year Outcome of Glaucoma Drainage Device Surgery After Penetrating Keratoplasty
evidence.quote: Only 7 corneal grafts (17.5%) remained clear at last follow-up.

rationale: This tests a false patient-level join. Each source supplies an outcome for its own study population.
limitations: There is no basis here for either a positive overlap count or a count of zero.
